references.caption: The cursed treasure of Hernando Cortès contained 882 identical pieces of gold in a stone chest. This gold Aztec medallion, worn around Elizabeth Swann’s neck, is embossed with intricate details including a skull.
references.qualifiedScope: Front medallion face, circular silhouette, central skull, raised concentric relief, small suspension loop. No rear, chain length, exact depth or microscopic glyph authority.

observations: Circular worn-gold silhouette, central skull, concentric relief and small suspension loop remain recognizable.
At 24–32 px the object reads as a gold token; peer review recommends 64 px for an identifiable skull, or 48 px with a native text label.
No wearer, extra necklace chain, attack, text, magic glow or additional gameplay action.
limitations: Micro-reliefs, skull-to-ring proportions and exact engraving layout are approximate.
The source is a display photograph, not a calibrated orthographic scan.
No proof of rear, thickness, animation, exact palette or full film-wide 1:1 fidelity.
Reliefs are simplified and unusually symmetric.
Eye sockets are rounder and more smiling than the source.
The top loop is thicker than the source.
Tiny red/orange points are visible along parts of the edge.
Inscriptions and exact reliefs cannot be verified from the icon.
